findings.title: Preserve not-attempted status when cancellation precedes an attempt
findings.body: Cancellation or deadline expiry can occur after a slot becomes `attempting` but before Fetcher appends its durable attempt, including during start-spacing sleep. This handler unconditionally changes that slot to `interrupted`. Parent recovery then leaves it unchanged because `reconcile_results` only handles `attempting` and `not_attempted` records. The final outcomes therefore report an interrupted request with no corresponding attempt, violating the protocol's distinction between cancellation before and after a durable attempt. Determine the status from the matching ledger entry, or reconcile these interrupted slots against the ledger after child exit.

overall_explanation: The cancellation path can misclassify an unattempted representation as interrupted, leaving outcome statuses inconsistent with the durable request ledger. Review used read-only inspection; no tests, acquisition, transforms, or nested reviewers were run.
